experiment.name: DaSelva category-blind clone-first comparison V2
experiment.authorizedScope: V2 document and validation-fixture work only
notAuthorized: model, image, clone, or website generation
creation of the V2 output root
modification or deletion of V1 outputs and evidence
shared database, plan, board, node, preference, cohort, or assessment writes
commit, push, deployment, or production enablement

inheritsWithoutChange: DaSelva semantic authority and source precedence
green, off-white, and terracotta target palette
claim, proof, location, menu, pricing, and booking exclusions
required routes, anchors, accessibility, and runtime constraints
baseFixture.authorityRule: The base fixture remains semantic authority. V2 changes only reference selection, fidelity method, strategy construction, taste gates, scoring, budget, and isolated output paths.

userCalibration.v1Assessment: C showed the best taste and consistency, but no strategy clearly won because each had meaningful strengths and weaknesses.
userCalibration.wFailure: W lost visual taste by the end of the process. Motion ambition did not compensate for a weak final static design.
userCalibration.methodCorrection: The desired output starts from a close clone of the reference and then replaces key assets: typography, palette, imagery, identity, target copy, and commercial behavior.
userCalibration.categoryFinding: V1 retained a latent food and hospitality bias. V2 gives business category zero scoring weight and audits the candidate pool before role allocation.

experimentQuestion: Under the same DaSelva target truth and media, which clone-first construction strategy preserves the strongest recognizable reference geometry and motion while producing the most tasteful, coherent target transformation?

selectionOrder: retrieve by observable composition, motion, responsive, and art-direction capabilities
freeze a diverse candidate pool before strategy allocation
score candidates without a category dimension
assign strategy roles from the scored evidence and compatibility constraints
capabilityQueries: radical full-page grid with preserved mobile transformation
cinematic image-led hero with measurable temporal choreography
unusual but coherent navigation and section rhythm
sticky or pinned narrative with native-scroll fallback
distinctive type-scale geometry that survives a font swap
content capacity for seven target movements without template repetition

candidatePool.rule: Diversity is an anti-bias audit, not a relevance score. A candidate is never promoted because its category resembles DaSelva.

scoreWeights.dimension: static visual taste and compositional confidence
cloneability of geometry and responsive structure
runtime independence and local reconstruction feasibility

allocationRules: No exact reference may appear in more than one strategy.
S receives the strongest complete single-page candidate, not the most category-adjacent candidate.
C receives one primary whose global spine is sufficiently complete without donors; donors repair only documented subsystem gaps.
W receives two or three scene references only when their post-swap static geometries can share one target-owned visual grammar.
If category-adjacent references exceed one of the three primaries, stop for a written bias audit before freezing Gate B.

cloneFirstContract.baselineRule: Reconstruct the selected reference page or scene locally at high fidelity before applying DaSelva assets. The baseline is a method artifact, not a publishable deliverable.
preserve: grid, proportions, anchoring, overlap, density, and whitespace rhythm
scroll authority, pinning, trigger positions, choreography, tempo, and easing character
media framing, cropping logic, and focal hierarchy
unusual or risky decisions that give the reference its identity
replaceAfterBaseline: brand name, logo, marks, copy, and factual content
all photography, video, illustration, iconography, and decorative source assets
commercial destinations, forms, booking behavior, addresses, claims, proof, and product identity

geometry.rule: Measure against matched reference screenshots before asset swap. Content-fit exceptions require a named divergence record rather than silent normalization.

motion.fallbackRule: Reduced-motion and unsupported-runtime paths preserve target content and conversion even when the reference lacks an equivalent fallback.

allowed: removal of source-specific commerce or identity
mobile compensation required to preserve content order
notAllowed: replacing distinctive geometry with a familiar landing-page pattern
simplifying motion because the implementation is difficult
borrowing a repair from another strategy after seeing its output
using target business category as a reason to normalize the reference
adaptationPolicy.divergenceRule: If target truth cannot fit without exceeding a fidelity tolerance or losing essential content, stop and ask how to proceed.

cloneFirstContract.provenanceRule: Each output preserves baseline evidence, an asset-swap ledger, a Reference Influence Ledger, and an explicit divergence log.

strategies.name: single-reference clone and asset swap
strategies.contract: Clone one full reference closely, validate the baseline, then replace target-owned assets and content without redesigning the reference into a conventional restaurant page.

strategies.name: primary chassis clone with bounded donor transplants
strategies.contract: Clone the primary reference as the complete global page. A donor enters only after its named subsystem is independently cloned and only when the primary has a documented gap.

donorMayOwn: one index, navigation, or transition subsystem
donorMayNotOwn: more than one major subsystem per donor

strategies.name: scene-clone synthesis with a static taste stop
strategies.contract: Clone each selected scene before synthesis. Apply target swaps, compose one motion-free desktop and mobile page, and stop for taste approval before implementing any motion.

requiredBoards: full-page desktop board with final target typography, palette, media, and copy
full-page mobile board with final target typography, palette, media, and copy
hero, Banda, and one cross-scene transition detail at native review size
dimensions: specificity and absence of generic AI patterns
staticTasteGate.failureRule: If W0 fails, preserve it as a V2 result. Do not add motion, polish through animation, or borrow C's design system. A new W board requires a separately labeled round.

requiredMethodArtifacts: independent baseline clone for every selected scene
motion-free W0 desktop and mobile boards
motion storyboard created only after W0 approval

sharedTargetMediaPolicy.rule: All V2 strategies receive byte-identical copies of the existing pack. Crop and placement may follow each reference, but no strategy may generate or receive extra target media.

perStrategyCallEnvelope: up to four bounded fidelity, responsive, or polish repairs

costCeiling.rule: This is a proposed hard ceiling, not spending approval. Gate C requires the frozen Gate B bundle, explicit budget approval, and the exact Gate C token.

hardValidity: baseline clone evidence exists before target swap
clone fidelity tolerances pass or every divergence is explicitly approved
production build and both target routes work
target semantic authority and prohibited-claim rules pass
no source identity, copy, asset, code, or runtime hotlink remains in the final output
all target media is local and byte-identical to the shared pack
no broken images, unexpected external runtime requests, console errors, or page-level overflow
keyboard, focus, reduced-motion, and responsive behavior preserve content and conversion
W cannot proceed past its static W0 board without human approval

weightedScore.dimension: static visual taste and art direction

qualityFloor.rule: Motion cannot raise a failing static-taste score. A hard-validity failure disqualifies the output even when its weighted total passes.

qualityRubric.comparisonRule: Judge baseline fidelity first, static target taste second, and motion third. Never let animation conceal a weak still frame.

A.scope: Freeze this contract, rubric, budgets, output paths, and failure policy.
A.exit: Manifest parses, validates, and has a stable external lock.

B.scope: Run category-blind read-only retrieval, score the frozen candidate pool, select references, and capture bounded visual, responsive, motion, runtime, and provenance evidence.
B.exit: One reviewed reference bundle with exact IDs, URLs, evidence, allocation, and bias audit. No clone or generated site.

C.scope: Build baseline clones, verify fidelity, swap target assets, and produce three isolated outputs. W pauses at W0 for explicit human approval before motion.
C.exit: S and C are runnable; W is runnable after W0 approval or preserved as a static failed/inconclusive result.

D.scope: Capture matched evidence and compare fidelity, taste, target fit, coherence, motion, accessibility, cost, provenance, and complexity.
D.exit: Evidence-backed ranking or an explicit inconclusive result.

E.scope: Choose a product direction without inferring deployment or production enablement.
E.exit: One recorded decision and separately scoped implementation follow-up.

rules: V1 remains immutable and available on ports 4311, 4312, and 4313.
No V2 directory may be created during Gate A or Gate B.
Every baseline clone and final target output has its own subdirectory and provenance record.
No strategy output, plan, token set, component, or repair advice may be copied into another strategy.
Do not commit, push, deploy, or write shared product state without separate approval.

failClosedWhen: the base manifest, target source, or shared media hash drifts
the Gate B candidate pool was selected with category terms or category scoring
a selected reference lacks desktop, mobile, or claimed motion evidence
a baseline clone exceeds fidelity tolerances without an approved divergence
target content cannot fit without material semantic loss
W static boards fail taste review
a strategy would exceed its call, time, or credit ceiling
an output path or port is owned by unknown work
onFailure: preserve baseline, target output, evidence, costs, and failure state
do not donate budget or references to another strategy
do not repair by copying the most successful strategy
label any retry as a new comparison round
rollback: All V2 generated work remains outside the product worktree.
V1 outputs are never overwritten or deleted.
No shared database or production rollback is expected because those writes are forbidden.

gateTransitions.gateAExit: The V2 manifest validates and its lock hash is stable.
gateTransitions.gateBRequires: Separate explicit approval using the exact Gate B token from manifest.lock.json.
gateTransitions.gateCRequires: Approved Gate B reference bundle hash, confirmed reuse of the frozen target-media pack, approved 1,425-credit ceiling, and the exact Gate C token.
gateTransitions.gateDRequires: Three preserved V2 results, including an explicitly failed or inconclusive W when W0 does not pass.
